Subject: GCP private offer — commit release schedule and invoicing cadence

Hi Mina / Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks for taking time last week. Our procurement team asked for a concrete drawdown schedule for the private offer so they can align invoice timing with our quarterly budgets. High level asks from their side:

- A proposed cadence for committing against the offer (monthly vs quarterly buckets)
- How Redwood will release credits/commit in GCP (single redemption vs staged releases)
- Invoicing cadence and whether Redwood can provide a consolidated invoice mapping to GCP SKU usage

I attached a short template our FP&A team prefers for milestone-aligned drawdowns. Can you confirm what you typically recommend for customers of our size (expecting ~$450k/year commit in year 1)? Also, we need to confirm lead GCP partner seller contact and co-sell attribution process so our field team is looped.

Thanks — aiming to present to procurement Tuesday.

Michael
Michael Yates
Head of Cloud Partnerships
CloudWave Analytics

Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: GCP private offer — commit release schedule and invoicing cadence

Hi Michael — thanks, and appreciated the template. Draft proposal below (high level), happy to iterate: 

1) Commit release pattern (recommended)
   - Phase 1 (Q1): 25% of annual committed dollars available as upfront redemption to cover ramp (applied immediately in GCP private offer)
   - Phase 2 (Q2–Q3): 50% released in two equal tranches (25% each) tied to usage thresholds and simple acceptance criteria (SKU burn targets)
   - Phase 3 (Q4): Remaining 25% held as final tranche for year-end true-up / overage protection

Rationale: staged releases help avoid front-loaded vendor spend while giving CloudWave runway during integration. We typically see this pattern with similar mid-market customers.

2) Invoicing cadence
   - Redwood issues a consolidated monthly invoice to CloudWave that maps to (a) Redwood commitment consumed, and (b) corresponding GCP redemption events (we include SKU-level breakout).
   - Net 30 standard; if procurement needs Net 45/60 we can escalate to finance (may affect pricing).

3) Co-sell / GCP partner contact
   - Lead Redwood co-sell contact: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.ai). She will coordinate with the assigned GCP seller.

Attached: initial commit schedule (redwood_commit_schedule_v1.xlsx) and one-page PO terms summary.

Next steps: If procurement is comfortable with staged release, we can generate the private offer paperwork (DocuSign) and share a proposed redemption timeline to route with GCP. I can also schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk procurement through the mechanics.

—Mina

Mina / Michael — procurement here. A few clarifying items before exec sign-off: 

- Can Redwood confirm how staged redemption appears in GCP billing (will CloudWave see multiple private-offer redemptions or a single aggregated credit?)
- We need a single Redwood legal contact to accept PO terms (we will route our standard T&Cs and prefer electronic signature).
- Please confirm whether Redwood can provide a monthly CSV export we can ingest (SKU, usage, credit_applied) — this is a hard requirement for our accounting system.

If those three are confirmed we can lock the timeline and route for signature.

Procurement Team

Adding quick answers from Redwood side: 

- How staged redemption shows up in GCP: each tranche is redeemed as an independent redemption event tied to the private offer. CloudWave will see multiple redemption transactions in GCP (we include a reconciliation sheet on our invoices to map redemptions to the commitment schedule).

- Legal contact & signature: legal@redwood.ai will be the contact for PO/T&Cs. We can send a DocuSign envelope (link below) to expedite.

- Monthly CSV export: yes — we produce a monthly usage CSV with SKU, tokens/units, credit_applied, and raw GCP SKU IDs. We can share a sample export this afternoon.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/ABC-CloudWave-PO-2027
Sample CSV export (internal drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-co-sell-docs

Mina — happy to take the lead on the DocuSign and follow up once procurement confirms acceptance of staged redemptions.

—Marissa
